# frontier-connector-abaqus

Reads Abaqus .fil results, .odb exports and .inp decks, and CalculiX .frd results. Reading .odb needs the exporter script and a licensed Abaqus installation.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install abaqus
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info abaqus
```

## Status

`verified-public-sample`. Reads Abaqus .fil results (ASCII and binary; Abaqus 6.19 and 6.23), .inp decks (mesh, sets, instances, includes) and CalculiX .frd results (ASCII and binary). .fil integration point values are averaged per element; section points, values at element nodes and contact / energy records are not read. Not read: .dat, .rpt, .sim, substructures, assembly-level sets that mix instances. The .odb route (odb_export.py) is not validated against a licensed Abaqus installation. .fil eigenmodes and continued SDV records are validated on generated files only.

## Getting the data out

Results: add *FILE FORMAT, ASCII with *NODE FILE / *EL FILE to the deck and convert the .fil results file; Abaqus is not needed to read it. Existing .odb: get the script with `python -m frontier_connectors exporters abaqus`, run `abaqus python odb_export.py job.odb --out job_frontier` and convert the job_frontier directory. Input decks (.inp) are read directly as mesh-only samples.

## Requirements and licence

Licence: Apache-2.0.

# frontier-connector-acusolve

Reads AcuSolve problem directories: the acuTrans EnSight export, the input deck and the run log. Experimental: not validated against a licensed AcuSolve installation.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install acusolve
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info acusolve
```

AcuSolve keeps results in `ACUSIM.DIR`, which is not read. Translate a run with `acuTrans`, then
point the connector at the problem directory:

```bash
acuTrans -pb pipe -to ensight -ensopt gold -mesh -out -extout -ts A
python -m frontier_connectors describe .
python -m frontier_connectors convert . --out ds
```

| File | Used for |
|---|---|
| `<problem>.<run>.case` + `ENSIGHT.DIR/` | mesh and fields, steady and transient (`ensight` connector) |
| `<problem>.<run>.echo`, else `<problem>.inp` | analysis type, equations, turbulence model, materials, `SIMPLE_BOUNDARY_CONDITION`s, solver settings; every command kept raw in `metadata["input"]` |
| `<problem>.<run>.Log` | time steps, residual and solution ratio history per variable, errors, header values |
| `Acusim.cnf`, `frontier_export.json` | problem name, run, case file |

The newest translated run is used; `options={"run": n}` picks another. Without an export the
connector raises `NeedsExportError` with the `acuTrans` command. `.inp` files of other tools are
not claimed.

Limitations:

- The run log format is undocumented; lines the parser does not know are collected generically.
- Parts are matched to boundary conditions by name; the match is not validated.
- H3D (`-to h3d`) is proprietary and not read.

## Status

`exporter+reader`. Experimental. Reads the acuTrans EnSight export through the `ensight` connector, physics and boundary conditions from the input deck and convergence from the run log. ACUSIM.DIR and H3D are not read. Not validated on a complete AcuSolve export; the export script is not validated against a licensed AcuSolve installation.

## Getting the data out

In the problem directory run `acuTrans -pb <problem> -to ensight -ensopt gold -mesh -out -extout -ts A`, or the wrapper script from `python -m frontier_connectors exporters acusolve`, then point the connector at the problem directory. Fields come from the EnSight export, physics and boundary conditions from <problem>.inp, convergence from <problem>.<run>.Log.

## Requirements and licence

Licence: Apache-2.0.

# frontier-connector-ansys

Reads CFX exports (CGNS or EnSight with a sidecar, CFD-Post CSV) and Mechanical / MAPDL .rst and .rth results. The CFX export scripts need a licensed CFX installation and are not validated against one.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install ansys
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info ansys
```

## Status

**`ansys-rst`** (`verified-public-sample`): Reads the mesh, the nodal DOF solution (displacement, rotation, temperature, ...) and nodal stress and elastic, plastic and thermal strain of every result set. Modal results use the mode number as axis, with the frequencies in the metadata; options={'deformed': true} adds the displacement to the points. Element-centred results and cyclic-symmetry expansion are not read. .rmg is not validated.

**`cfx`** (`exporter+reader`): Experimental. Reads CFD-Post generic CSV exports (point clouds, [Faces] surfaces, [Lines] polylines, null values) and CFX profile data ([Spatial Fields], [Parameters]) as single files, and cfx5export CGNS / EnSight directories with the frontier_export.json sidecar. The cfx5export route and the exporter scripts are not validated against a licensed CFX installation; the sidecar (version, domains, boundary types, fluid, turbulence model) is validated on generated files only. .res, .def, .trn, .bak and .cfx are proprietary and not read.

## Getting the data out

**`ansys-rst`**: Point at the file.rst / file.rth that Mechanical or MAPDL writes into the solver files directory (pip install 'frontier-connector-ansys[rst]'). For results the open reader cannot expand (cyclic symmetry, distributed files) use the DPF script: `python -m frontier_connectors exporters ansys_mechanical`.

**`cfx`**: Run `sh export_for_frontier.sh -o export_dir run_001.res` (script: `python -m frontier_connectors exporters cfx`; it wraps cfx5export -cgns and writes frontier_export.json), or play export_for_frontier.cse in CFD-Post, then point the connector at the export directory. A single CSV exported from CFD-Post is read directly.

## Requirements and licence

Licence: Apache-2.0. Installs `vtk>=9.3`.

| Optional package | Licence | Used to | Note |

| `ansys-mapdl-reader` | MIT | read .rst/.rth result files without an Ansys licence |  |

# frontier-connector-arrays

Reads NetCDF 3/4, generic HDF5 and Zarr v2/v3. Common layouts are detected automatically; any other layout takes a mapping config.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install arrays
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info arrays
```

## Status

**`hdf5`** (`verified-public-sample`): Detects datasets with dimension scales, The Well, PDEBench / FNO-style grids and points + cells mesh layouts. Any other layout needs a mapping config: the error prints the dataset tree and a mapping skeleton. The Well, dimension-scale and mesh layouts are validated on generated files only. Fluent CFF, CGNS, MATLAB v7.3, VTKHDF, Exodus, XDMF heavy data, MED and PyFR files belong to their own connectors.

**`netcdf`** (`verified-public-sample`): NetCDF-4 is read with h5py, NetCDF-3 classic and 64-bit-offset with scipy (memory-mapped). CF grids with 1-D coordinates and UGRID 2-D face meshes are detected automatically. Curvilinear grids, CDF-5, UGRID 1-D / 3-D-layered and DSG feature types need a mapping or options={'engine': 'xarray'}.

**`zarr`** (`verified-synthetic`): Reads directory and .zip stores in Zarr v2 and v3. Dimension names come from _ARRAY_DIMENSIONS (v2) or dimension_names (v3); CF attributes are honoured as for NetCDF. Remote stores (s3://, gs://) are not opened. Validated on generated files only.

## Getting the data out

**`hdf5`**: Write the arrays with h5py / HDF5 from any solver or script, then describe the layout with a mapping config (--mapping file.json) unless it is one of the auto-detected layouts (dimension scales, PDEBench, The Well, points+cells+fields).

**`netcdf`**: Most climate/ocean/weather models and many CFD codes write NetCDF directly; from Python use xarray.Dataset.to_netcdf, from ParaView/VisIt use the NetCDF writer. OPeNDAP URLs, GRIB and multi-file datasets go through options={'engine': 'xarray'}.

**`zarr`**: xarray: Dataset.to_zarr(path). Any zarr group written by a solver or script can be described with a mapping config. A frontier-dataset directory (or one of its sample stores) is read back as-is.

## Requirements and licence

Licence: Apache-2.0. Installs `h5py>=3.10`, `scipy>=1.13`, `zarr>=3.0`.

| Optional package | Licence | Used to | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `xarray` | Apache-2.0 | open GRIB, OPeNDAP and multi-file datasets (engine=xarray) |  |

# frontier-connector-catalyst

Reads Conduit Mesh Blueprint steps from a spool directory, Conduit relay files or ADIOS2 (BP5 / SST), during or after the run. Not validated against ParaView Catalyst.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install catalyst
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info catalyst
```

A running solver feeds a Frontier dataset step by step. The unit of exchange is the Conduit Mesh
Blueprint tree, the same tree a ParaView Catalyst 2 adaptor passes under
`catalyst/channels/<name>/data`.

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors import catalyst run/spool --out dataset --option timeout=600
python -m frontier_connectors import catalyst run/spool --out dataset --dry-run
python -m frontier_connectors convert run/spool --out dataset      # after the run
```

## What it reads

| Source | Written by | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| spool directory, `frontier-spool` v1 (`frontier-stream.json`, `step_<n>.npz`, `frontier-stream.done`) | `frontier_emit.py` in the solver or in the Catalyst pipeline script, both in `exporter-catalyst` | numpy |
| Conduit relay Blueprint series (`<name>.cycle_<n>.root` + domain files; hdf5, json, yaml, conduit_json, conduit_base64_json, conduit_bin) | `conduit.relay.io.blueprint.save_mesh`, Ascent relay extracts | `h5py` for hdf5, `pyyaml` for yaml; Conduit itself is not needed |
| ADIOS2 BP4 / BP5 file (also while written) or SST stream | variables named by Blueprint path, or the Fides predefined-model attributes | `adios2` (Apache-2.0) |
| `conduit.Node` or nested `dict` in memory | `frontier_connector_catalyst.blueprint.mesh_to_samples`, `StepConverter` | LLNL Conduit only for `Node` objects |

Files a Catalyst pipeline writes with plain VTK extractors (`.vtpd`, `.vtm`, VTKHDF) are read by
the `vtk` connector.

## Blueprint coverage

- Coordsets: `uniform`, `rectilinear`, `explicit` (Cartesian).
- Topologies: `points`, `uniform`, `rectilinear`, `structured`, `unstructured` with
  `point line tri quad tet hex wedge pyramid`, `polygonal`, `polyhedral` (with `subelements`) and
  `mixed` (`shape_map`).
- Fields: `vertex` or `element`, scalar or mcarray, `units`.
- `state/{time,cycle,domain_id}`, multi-domain trees, Catalyst `mesh` and `multimesh` channels.

Uniform and rectilinear topologies become `grid` samples, all-2-D topologies `surface`
(triangulated, cell data follows), point topologies `point_cloud`, the rest `mesh`. One zone per
(domain, topology); MPI-decomposed domains stay separate zones.

Not supported: non-Cartesian coordsets, strided structured topologies, high-order meshes and
fields. Skipped with a warning: material fields, matsets, specsets, adjsets, nestsets.

## Following a live stream

`--option follow=true` (the importer's default) tails the source. Each step is yielded once, in
increasing step number, and only when complete; the dataset is appended along time.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `timeout` | 60 | seconds without a new complete step before giving up; also the wait for the stream to appear |
| `poll` | 0.2 | seconds between looks |
| `until` | `done-marker` | `timeout`: ignore end markers, stop after `timeout` idle seconds (relay series) |
| `on_timeout` | `stop` | keep what arrived; `error` raises and leaves no dataset |
| `on_restart` | `skip` | steps re-emitted after a restart from a checkpoint are not read twice; `error` raises |
| `order_grace` | 2 | seconds to wait for a step the producer's `prev` chain says is missing |
| `partial_grace` | 5 | seconds an unreadable visible file may stay unchanged before it is declared corrupt |
| `settle` | 0.5 | seconds a relay file must be unmodified before it is read |
| `max_steps` | - | stop after N steps |
| `geometry` | `changed` | `always` sends the mesh with every step (needed with `--time-as-samples` for changing topology) |
| `name` | - | relay series base name when a directory holds several |
| `engine`, `adios_parameters`, `fides_order` | `BPFile`, -, `zyx` | ADIOS2 engine (`BP5`, `BP4`, `SST`), engine parameters, grid array order of Fides models |

While following, `--times` accepts `all` or a forward range `start:stop:step`. Timeouts,
restarts, lost steps and failed end markers are logged and added to the conversion warnings.
Hidden `.<name>.tmp-<pid>` files are never read. A visible file that does not decode is retried.

## ADIOS2 variable convention

Each Blueprint array is a variable named by its path (`coordsets/coords/values/x`,
`topologies/mesh/elements/connectivity`, `fields/T/values`, `state/time`, `state/cycle`), and
each string leaf an attribute (`topologies/mesh/type = "unstructured"`,
`fields/T/association = "vertex"`, `fields/T/units = "K"`). The mesh may be written in the first
step only. Several domains share a prefix (`fluid/coordsets/...`). The attributes
`frontier/solver`, `frontier/solver_version`, `frontier/domain` and `frontier/time_units` go to
the dataset metadata. The Fides predefined models `uniform`, `rectilinear`,
`unstructured_single` and `unstructured` are translated; the Fides JSON file, XGC and GTC are not.

## Status

`verified-synthetic`. Reads frontier-spool directories, Conduit relay Blueprint files (hdf5, json, yaml, conduit_*) and ADIOS2 BP4 / BP5 files and BP5 / SST streams, during or after the run. Validated with Conduit 0.9.5 and ADIOS2 2.12.1. Not validated against ParaView Catalyst (the pipeline script), Fides or MPI-parallel writers.

## Getting the data out

Get the solver-side scripts with `python -m frontier_connectors plugins install exporter-catalyst`, then use one of: (1) copy frontier_emit.py (numpy only) next to the solver and call Emitter.write_step(step, time, blueprint_mesh) at each output step; (2) run the Catalyst 2 pipeline frontier_catalyst_pipeline.py (CATALYST_IMPLEMENTATION_NAME=paraview), which writes the same spool; (3) write Conduit relay Blueprint files (relay.io.blueprint.save_mesh, Ascent) or ADIOS2 BP5 / SST with Blueprint paths as variable names. Follow the run with `python -m frontier_connectors import catalyst <spool|stream> --out ds`. Files a Catalyst pipeline writes with plain VTK extractors (.vtpd / .vtm series, VTKHDF) are read by the `vtk` connector.

## Requirements and licence

Licence: Apache-2.0.

| Optional package | Licence | Used to | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `adios2` | Apache-2.0 | read ADIOS2 BP4/BP5 files and follow BP5/SST streams |  |
| `h5py` | BSD-3-Clause | read Conduit relay Blueprint files written with the hdf5 protocol |  |
| `pyyaml` | MIT | read Conduit relay Blueprint files written with the yaml protocol |  |
| `conduit` | BSD-3-Clause | pass conduit.Node objects to the Blueprint bridge directly | LLNL Conduit is not on PyPI (the PyPI project named conduit is unrelated): build it from https://github.com/LLNL/conduit or use Spack |

# frontier-connector-cgns

Reads CGNS/HDF5 with h5py and ADF files through VTK.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install cgns
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info cgns
```

## Status

`verified-public-sample`. Reads CGNS/HDF5 with h5py: structured and unstructured zones, linear and quadratic elements, MIXED, NGON_n / NFACE_n, boundary patches as surface zones, vertex and cell-centred solutions, rind, links, FlowSolutionPointers, file-per-step series, units, reference state and flow equations. Cubic and higher elements, face-centred solutions and non-Cartesian coordinates are not supported. ADF files and options={'engine': 'vtk'} go through VTK's vtkCGNSReader, without the CGNS metadata.

## Getting the data out

Export CGNS from the solver or post-processor (Ansys CFX: cfx5export -cgns; Fluent: File > Export > CGNS; STAR-CCM+: File > Export > CGNS; Fidelity/FINE, SU2, elsA, Pointwise write it natively) and point at the .cgns file or a directory holding a numbered series.

Licence: Apache-2.0. Installs `h5py>=3.10`, `vtk>=9.3`.

plugins.readme:
# frontier-connector-fidelity

Reads Fidelity / FINE projects: the CGNS solution plus .run, .iec, .res and .xmf metadata. Validated on generated files only.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install fidelity
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info fidelity
```

FINE/Turbo, FINE/Open, FINE/Marine and Fidelity write their solution as CGNS. This plugin reads
the project layout, hands the CGNS file to the `cgns` connector and adds the metadata stored
next to it.

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors describe my-project/my-project_design/my-project_design.run
python -m frontier_connectors convert my-project --out ds --option computation=design
```

Accepted paths: a `.run` file, a computation directory, the `.iec` project file, the project
directory, or a `.cfv` / `.me.cfv` file of a computation.

| File | Used for |
|---|---|
| `<project>_<computation>.cgns` | mesh and fields (bases `project3d`, `project3d_solid_data`, ...) |
| `<...>_t<i>.cgns` (two or more) | unsteady series, one step per file; `options={"unsteady": False}` reads the final solution instead |
| `.res` | turbulence model, steady or unsteady, iteration count, residual history |
| `.iec` | version, project type, grid file, computations |
| `.xmf` | global results (stations, mass flow, performance), kept as a generic tree |
| `.run` | every keyword kept raw in `metadata["run"]`; boundary-condition-like blocks in `boundary_conditions` |

Zones without `GridCoordinates_t` (the restart base `fluid_solution`) are listed in
`metadata["zones_without_mesh"]` and skipped. A file with only that base raises
`NeedsExportError`: select output quantities in the Outputs page and rerun.

`.run` keywords are not publicly documented. Rotation speed, time step, fluid and similar
settings are looked up by keyword name (`metadata["keyword_hints"]`) and promoted to `physics`
or `parameters` only when a single value matches; `metadata["keyword_mapping"]` says which
keyword was used.

Validated on generated files only, written from the FINE/Turbo user manual (project files with
`VERSION 8.2`). Newer Fidelity releases may lay out projects differently.

## Status

`verified-synthetic`. Reads mesh and fields from the solver's CGNS file through the `cgns` connector, steady or as a <name>_t<i>.cgns series; zones without a mesh (the restart base) are skipped. Metadata comes from the .iec project file, the .res residual history and the .xmf global results. .run keywords are undocumented: kept raw, with name-based hints only. Validated on generated files only, not on a real FINE or Fidelity project.

## Getting the data out

FINE/Turbo, FINE/Open, FINE/Marine and Fidelity write the solution as <project>_<computation>.cgns next to the .run file: point at the .run file, the computation directory, the .iec file or the project directory. Select the 3-D output quantities you need in the Outputs page before running (they go to the CGNS file together with the mesh).

## Requirements and licence

Licence: Apache-2.0.

# frontier-connector-fluent

Reads Fluent CFF (.cas.h5 / .dat.h5) and legacy .cas / .dat files without Ansys software. Live PyFluent sessions and batch journals need a licensed Fluent installation and are not validated against one.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install fluent
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info fluent
```

## Live sessions and batch journals (`fluent-live`)

```bash
# session spec -> export through PyFluent -> dataset (needs ansys-fluent-core and a licensed Fluent)
python -m frontier_connectors import fluent-live run.fluent.json --dry-run
python -m frontier_connectors import fluent-live run.fluent.json --out dataset
# without PyFluent: a journal bundle for `fluent 3ddp -g -t<N> -i export.jou`
python -m frontier_connector_fluent journal run.fluent.json --out export_dir
python -m frontier_connectors convert export_dir --out dataset
```

## Status

**`fluent-cff`** (`verified-public-sample`): Reads Fluent 19.4 to 24.1 CFF files with h5py. Cell zones are read by default; boundary zones with options={'boundaries': True} or zones=[...].

**`fluent-legacy`** (`verified-public-sample`): Read through VTK's vtkFLUENTReader: cell zones are volume meshes. For a face zone VTK returns the adjacent cells carrying the face values, not the faces, so boundary zones are off by default. Polyhedral cases are not supported.

**`fluent-live`** (`implemented-unverified-live`): Experimental. Not validated against a licensed Fluent installation. Written for the PyFluent 0.42.2 API (Fluent 2025 R1 and 2026 R1). Journal path: the answer order of export/ensight-gold and export/cgns is undocumented and marked unverified in the generated journal.

## Getting the data out

**`fluent-cff`**: Fluent 2020R1+: File > Write > Case & Data writes .cas.h5/.dat.h5 (CFF is the default; TUI: /file/cff-files? yes, /file/write-case-data name). For transients set File > Write > Autosave so that one .dat.h5 per saved time step is written.

**`fluent-legacy`**: Fluent: /file/cff-files? no then File > Write > Case & Data writes legacy .cas/.dat; prefer the CFF default (.cas.h5/.dat.h5), which carries real boundary surfaces.

**`fluent-live`**: Write a session spec run.fluent.json (case, data files, export format cff | ensight | cgns, zones, quantities). With PyFluent and a licensed Fluent: `python -m frontier_connectors import fluent-live run.fluent.json --out dataset` (--dry-run lists every call). Without PyFluent: `python -m frontier_connector_fluent journal run.fluent.json --out export_dir` writes export.jou and launch scripts for `fluent 3ddp -g -t<N> -i export.jou`; run it, then convert export_dir. Ready-made scripts: `python -m frontier_connectors exporters fluent`.

## Requirements and licence

Licence: Apache-2.0. Installs `h5py>=3.10`, `vtk>=9.3`.

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors import luminary <simulation-id> --out ds             # download and convert
python -m frontier_connector_luminary list projects                           # projects | simulations (project=) | meshes (project=) | solutions (simulation=)
```

Source: `<simulation id>`, the path of a `*.luminary.json` reference file, or `list:<kind>` with
`--option project=<id>` and similar for the ids. A listing run through `import` without
`--out` is written to `listing.json` in the download directory.

Every call goes through the optional proprietary `luminarycloud` SDK (`pip install luminarycloud`);
Luminary Cloud has no public REST API. `--option solution=all` downloads the surface data of
every solution as one `.pvd` time series. Volume data exists only for completed steady
simulations.

Solver settings, boundary conditions and mesh statistics, where the service has them, go to the
source description and to every sample's `meta.json`. Downloaded files are read by the format
connectors (`vtk`, `ensight`, `cgns`, `tecplot`, ...). The `frontier_cloud.json` sidecar records
what was fetched and never contains the API key. With the optional `keyring` package, a key
stored as service `frontier-connectors`, user `LC_API_KEY` is used when the variable is not set.

`implemented-unverified-live`. Experimental. Not validated against the live Luminary Cloud service. An extracted .vtm / .vtu / .vtp directory is read offline through the `vtk` connector; validated on generated files only.

Run `python -m frontier_connectors import luminary <simulation id> --out ds` with LC_API_KEY set and `pip install luminarycloud` (--dry-run prints the SDK calls; --option solution=all for a transient surface series). # frontier-connector-matlab

Reads MAT-files v4 to v7.3 and GNU Octave text, binary and HDF5 save files, including the layouts of the +frontier export package. No MATLAB installation is needed.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install matlab
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info matlab
```

Two connectors share one reader:

- `matlab`: MAT-files level 4, 5 (v6, v7) and v7.3, written by MATLAB, GNU Octave or scipy.
- `octave`: GNU Octave's own save formats (`save -text`, `-binary`, `-hdf5`, also with `-z`),
  detected by content.

Both recognise the same layouts (the `+frontier` canonical layout, PDE Toolbox and `[p,e,t]`,
meshes, meshgrid and ndgrid arrays, snapshots, runs, ODE and Simulink signals) and take the same
mapping config.

## Status

**`matlab`** (`verified-public-sample`): Reads MAT-files level 4, 5, 6, 7 and v7.3 written by MATLAB (4.2c to 7.4, R2013 to R2025) and by GNU Octave 11.3.0. A sparse logical written by Octave is skipped with a warning. PDE Toolbox result structs and curvilinear grids are validated on generated files only. The +frontier export package is validated under GNU Octave 11.3.0 and not validated under MATLAB: Name=value call syntax, '-v7.3' writing, tables and timetables, string arrays, triangulation objects, PDE Toolbox result and model objects, and Simulink and Simscape objects. The matlab.engine live path is not validated.

**`octave`** (`verified-public-sample`): Reads GNU Octave's text, binary and HDF5 save formats, also gzip-compressed (-z); HDF5 arrays are read one time step at a time. Function handles and old-style @class objects are opaque. Not read: binary files from before Octave 2.1 and the pre-2004 HDF5 layout. Struct member order is lost in Octave's HDF5 files (sorted by name). Validated with files written by GNU Octave 11.3.0 only; big-endian binary files, narrowed storage codes of older binary files, text files without the 'Created by Octave' line and CRLF line ends are validated on generated files only.

## Getting the data out

**`matlab`**: Save plain arrays or structs with save(file, '-v7.3') in MATLAB or save('-v7', file) in GNU Octave. Tables, timetables, Simulink outputs and PDE result objects need the +frontier package: add the folder printed by `python -m frontier_connectors exporters matlab` to the path and call frontier.export(file, 'Name', value, ...), frontier.exportPDEResults or frontier.exportSimulink (MATLAB R2019b+ and GNU Octave 7+; Name=value syntax needs MATLAB R2021a+). The package writes '-v7.3' in MATLAB and '-v7' in Octave; above 2 GB per array in Octave use '-hdf5' and the octave connector.

**`octave`**: Nothing to install in Octave. Use save('-hdf5', file, ...) (any size, read lazily), save('-binary', file, ...) or save('-text', file, ...), also with -z, for plain arrays and structs in the same layouts as the matlab connector. save('-v7', file, ...) writes a MAT-file, read by the matlab connector. For explicit geometry, time and units use the +frontier package (`python -m frontier_connectors exporters matlab`): frontier.export(file, 'Nodes', p, 'Elements', t, 'Fields', struct('u', u), 'Version', '-hdf5').

## Requirements and licence

Licence: Apache-2.0. Installs `scipy>=1.13`, `h5py>=3.10`.

| Optional package | Licence | Used to | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `matlabengine` | LicenseRef-MathWorks-Proprietary | export through a live MATLAB session | proprietary; needs a licensed MATLAB |

# frontier-connector-meshio

Reads Exodus II, XDMF, Gmsh MSH and MED files, SU2 meshes, and the other mesh formats meshio supports.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install meshio
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info meshio
```

## Status

**`exodus`** (`verified-public-sample`): Element blocks are the default zones; side sets and node sets are extra zones. Reads nodal, element and global variables at all time steps. One piece of a parallel decomposition is read as it is, without merging.

**`gmsh`** (`verified-public-sample`): Physical groups become zones. $NodeData and $ElementData views are read, including several time steps of one view; element views assume the consecutive element tags Gmsh writes. $ElementNodeData and .pos parsed views are not read. MSH 4 files need every saved entity in a physical group. Views and binary files are validated on generated files only.

**`med`** (`verified-public-sample`): Groups (families) become zones; node groups are point-cloud zones. Reads fields on nodes and cells for every stored time step. Gauss-point (ELGA) and element-node (ELNO) fields are averaged per cell; their storage order for more than one cell is not validated on a real file. Fields on a profile are NaN outside it. Structured MED meshes and polyhedra are not read. Several time steps are validated on generated files only.

**`meshio`** (`verified-public-sample`): Reads Medit .mesh / .meshb, Netgen .vol, TetGen .node / .ele, UGRID and FLAC3D .f3grid. Region and material ids become zones. MOAB .h5m, DOLFIN XML, AVS-UCD, PERMAS, Kratos .mdpa and HMF are validated on meshio-written files only.

**`su2`** (`verified-public-sample`): Reads the mesh, markers as boundary zones and multi-zone meshes; solver, turbulence model, free-stream parameters and the boundary condition of each marker come from a .cfg next to the mesh. No solution fields.

**`xdmf`** (`verified-public-sample`): Unstructured grids and meshio time series are read through meshio; structured topologies (CoRect, Rect, SMesh), spatial collections and dolfinx / ParaView temporal collections through VTK's Xdmf2 reader. FiniteElementFunction (dolfinx checkpoint) attributes are not evaluated: only the mesh of such files is read. Cell-centred data of regular grids is averaged to the grid nodes.

## Getting the data out

**`exodus`**: MOOSE: [Outputs] exodus = true. Sierra/SEACAS/Cubit/libMesh write .e/.exo/.g directly; join parallel pieces (file.e.N.i) with SEACAS epu first.

**`gmsh`**: Gmsh: File > Export > .msh (version 4.1 or 2.2; tick 'Save all elements' only if you have no physical groups). Post-processing views: Save 'Mesh-based' views into the .msh; parsed-view .pos files must be re-saved that way.

**`med`**: Code_Aster: IMPR_RESU(FORMAT='MED', RESU=_F(RESULTAT=...)); Salome: File > Export > MED; Code_Saturne: writer format 'MED'. MED 2.1 files need Salome's medimport.

**`meshio`**: These are mesh formats: results usually live elsewhere (FUN3D: Tecplot/VTK, NGSolve: VTK, FEniCS: XDMF/PVD). Any other meshio format can be converted with `meshio convert in.xxx out.vtu` and read by the vtk connector.

**`su2`**: The .su2 file is the mesh only. SU2 results are written as VTU/PVD (OUTPUT_FILES= PARAVIEW), Tecplot, CSV (surface_flow.csv, restart_flow.csv) or CGNS: read those with the vtk, tecplot, tabular or cgns connectors.

**`xdmf`**: dolfinx: XDMFFile.write_mesh / write_function(u, t); legacy FEniCS: XDMFFile.write; ParaView: Save Data as Xdmf. Keep the .h5 heavy-data file next to the .xdmf.

## Requirements and licence

Licence: Apache-2.0. Installs `meshio>=5.3`, `vtk>=9.3`, `h5py>=3.10`.

# frontier-connector-optistruct

Reads OptiStruct .fem decks, OP2 and punch results and HyperView exports of .h3d, and Radioss / OpenRadioss animation files and starter decks. OP2 needs pyNastran; .h3d is not read directly.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install optistruct
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info optistruct
```

| Connector | Reads | How |
|---|---|---|
| `optistruct` | `.fem` deck | `nastran` deck reader plus the OptiStruct control section, `DTI,UNITS` and `$HMNAME` names |
| | `.pch` (`OUTPUT,PUNCH`) | built-in punch reader; mesh from `<job>.fem` |
| | `.op2` (`OUTPUT,OP2`, `PARAM,POST,-1`) | `nastran` connector (pyNastran, optional, pins numpy below 2) |
| | HyperView export directory | `frontier_hv_export.tcl` (plugin `exporter-optistruct`) plus CSV reader; mesh from `<job>.fem` |
| | `.h3d` | not read (proprietary): `NeedsExportError` names the routes above |
| `radioss` | `<run>A001 ...` animation files (plain or gzip) | built-in reader; the states of the run are the time axis |
| | `<run>_0000.rad` starter deck | mesh, units, parts, materials |
| | `<run>T01` time history | not read: convert with `th_to_csv`, then use the `tabular` connector |

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors describe job.pch                     # job.fem next to it
python -m frontier_connectors convert job.fem --out ds             # reads job.op2 / job.pch when present
python -m frontier_connectors convert job.fem --out mesh --option results=none
python -m frontier_connectors convert RUNA001 --out crash          # RUN_0000.rad next to it gives units
```

Samples follow the `nastran` connector: one zone per property (`pshell_2`, `psolid_1`), one
sample per subcase and zone (`<job>__subcase1__psolid_1`), modes or time steps as the time axis
(`TimeInfo.quantity` is `mode` or `time`). Radioss: one zone per part (`part_12`), moving points
per state, `displacement` derived from the first state, `element_status` is the raw erosion byte.

Options (`--option key=value`): every `nastran` option (`units`, `deformed`, `subcases`,
`plate_fiber`, `rotations`, `geometry`, `engine`) plus `results`
(`auto | op2 | pch | none | file`) for decks. Radioss: `deformed` (default true), `deck`.

Metadata read when the files sit next to the source: `<job>.out` (version, model size, mass,
iterations, objective history), `<job>.hist`, `<job>.desvar`, `<run>_0001.rad` (end time, `/ANIM`
requests).

## Status

**`optistruct`** (`verified-public-sample`): Reads .fem decks (mesh, control section, names), OP2 results through pyNastran (optional) and punch results with a built-in reader. PLY, STACK, DTPL and other OptiStruct-only cards are counted, not converted; complex, bar / beam and composite punch tables are skipped. .h3d is not read; the HyperView export route is not validated against a licensed HyperView installation. The punch reader is not validated on OptiStruct-written files (validated on MSC Nastran punch files and generated files). .out, .hist and .desvar metadata is validated on generated files only.

**`radioss`** (`verified-public-sample`): Reads animation files (magic 0x542c, plain or gzip) and starter decks (block format, 10-character fields): mesh, units, parts, materials. Quadratic solids are reduced to corner nodes; //SUBMODEL offsets and the 4x fixed format are not handled. Time history (T01) is not read: convert it with th_to_csv and read the CSV with `tabular`. Older animation versions and adaptive-mesh runs (changing topology) are rejected. Tensors, SPH and mass / numbering flags are validated on generated files only.

## Getting the data out

**`optistruct`**: Add `OUTPUT,PUNCH` (text <job>.pch, read natively) or `OUTPUT,OP2` / `PARAM,POST,-1` (<job>.op2, needs pyNastran) plus `DISPLACEMENT = ALL`, `STRESS = ALL` to the .fem deck and keep the deck next to the result file. .h3d is proprietary: rerun with one of the above, or export it from HyperView with frontier_hv_export.tcl (plugin exporter-optistruct) and read the export directory. Radioss: connector `radioss`.

**`radioss`**: Animation files: request them in the engine deck (/ANIM/DT plus /ANIM/VECT/VEL, /ANIM/ELEM/EPSP, /ANIM/TENS/STRESS/..., optionally /ANIM/GZIP) and point the connector at <run>A001; keep <run>_0000.rad next to it for units. Time history <run>T01: convert with the open th_to_csv tool and read the CSV with `tabular`. Radioss .h3d output is proprietary: write A-files instead (they are the default; drop /H3D/... only).

## Requirements and licence

| Optional package | Licence | Used to | Note |

| `pyNastran` | BSD-3-Clause | read OptiStruct OP2 results (OUTPUT,OP2) through the nastran connector | pins numpy<2; punch files (OUTPUT,PUNCH) need no extra package |

# frontier-connector-powerflow

Reads PowerFLOW surface measurement files (.snc) and pf2ens / PowerVIZ EnSight exports. Experimental: the .snc reader is validated on generated files only; .fnc files are not read.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install powerflow
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info powerflow
```

## What it reads

| Source | How |
|---|---|
| `.snc` surface measurement file | read directly (NetCDF classic; a NetCDF-4 / HDF5 container needs `h5py`) |
| export directory of `export_for_frontier.sh` (`pf2ens` EnSight Gold per frame, `nc_stats.txt`, `frontier_export.json`) | `ensight` connector, one step per frame |
| EnSight Gold export whose header names PowerVIZ, PowerINSIGHT or pf2ens | `ensight` connector |
| `.fnc`, `.cdi`, `.ckpt` | not read: `NeedsExportError` with the `pf2ens` command |

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors describe forces_rotor.snc
python -m frontier_connectors convert forces_rotor.snc --out ds --option time_step_seconds=2e-6
```

## The `.snc` reader

Dassault Systemes publishes no file specification. The layout follows the public project
[jmrendona/rotaris](https://github.com/jmrendona/rotaris) (PowerFLOW 6-2024 and 6-2025 files);
no code was copied.

- Every face with surfels is a surface zone. Surfel polygons are fan-triangulated
  (`face_parent` maps triangles back) and measurements are cell fields.
- Coordinates are multiplied by `LatticeLength` (metres). Variables of class
  `LatticeForcePerArea` are multiplied by `LatticeDensity * LatticeVelocity^2` (Pa), and
  `LatticeVelocity` and `LatticeDensity` by their scale. **Static pressure and every other class
  stay in lattice units** (`units == "lattice"`, with a warning); use the `pf2ens` route for
  pressure in physical units. `options={"lattice_units": True}` keeps everything raw.
- `X/Y/Z` triples (`Surface X-Force` ...) become one vector field. With a rotating reference
  frame the geometry is in the rotating frame and force vectors in the global frame
  (`metadata.rotating_frame` has axis, origin and angular rate; no rotation is applied).
- Frame times are the mid lattice time step of each frame (`units == "timestep"`). For seconds
  pass `options={"time_step_seconds": dt}`, or save the output of
  `exaritool nc-stats.ri <file> -detail` as `<file>.snc.nc_stats.txt`
  (`options={"nc_stats": path}`).
- A file shorter than its header says (a run still writing) is read up to the last complete
  frame, with a warning.

Not supported: `.fnc` fluid files, composite, probe and other measurement variants, and unit
classes other than those above.

## Status

`verified-synthetic`. Experimental. Dassault Systemes publishes no .snc specification; the reader is validated on generated files only. Geometry is in metres and force-per-area, velocity and density variables in SI; static pressure and other unit classes stay in lattice units, and frame times in lattice time steps unless nc-stats output is supplied. .fnc, .cdi and .ckpt are not read. The pf2ens export script is not validated against a licensed PowerFLOW installation.

## Getting the data out

Surface measurement files (.snc) are read directly. For fluid files (.fnc), and for static pressure in physical units, run `export_for_frontier.sh <file> <out_dir>` (script: `python -m frontier_connectors exporters powerflow`; it calls `pf2ens` per frame and `exaritool nc-stats.ri`) and point at the directory. Or export EnSight Gold from PowerVIZ and point at the .case file.

## Requirements and licence

Licence: Apache-2.0.

| Optional package | Licence | Used to | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `h5py` | BSD-3-Clause | read a measurement file stored in a NetCDF-4/HDF5 container |  |

Imports Rescale job outputs (REST v2): runs, software, design variables and filtered output file downloads; needs a Rescale account. Experimental: not validated against the live service.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install rescale
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info rescale
```

```bash
export RESCALE_API_KEY=...                 # read from the environment or the keyring, never from a file

python -m frontier_connectors import rescale <job-id> --out ds --dry-run   # print the calls
python -m frontier_connectors import rescale <job-id> --out ds             # download and convert
python -m frontier_connector_rescale list jobs                           # jobs | runs (job=) | files (job=, optionally run=)
```

Source: `<job id>`, the path of a `*.rescale.json` reference file, or `list:<kind>` with
`--option project=<id>` and similar for the ids. A listing run through `import` without
`--out` is written to `listing.json` in the download directory.

REST v2 with the standard library only. `RESCALE_API_URL` or `--option api_url=` selects a regional
platform such as `https://eu.rescale.com`. `--option include=*.vtu,*.case` and `exclude=` filter
the output files. Files land in `run<n>/...` and each run's design variables become sample
parameters. Files above 5 GB are refused (the Files API limit).

Solver settings, boundary conditions and mesh statistics, where the service has them, go to the
source description and to every sample's `meta.json`. Downloaded files are read by the format
connectors (`vtk`, `ensight`, `cgns`, `tecplot`, ...). The `frontier_cloud.json` sidecar records
what was fetched and never contains the API key. With the optional `keyring` package, a key
stored as service `frontier-connectors`, user `RESCALE_API_KEY` is used when the variable is not set.

## Status

`implemented-unverified-live`. Experimental. Not validated against the live Rescale service. REST v2: jobs, job status, runs with their design variables, paged run output files with include / exclude filters, file download. Mesh and boundary conditions come from the result files, which are read by the format connectors. Files above 5 GB are refused (the Files API limit). A downloaded job directory is read offline; validated on generated files only.

## Getting the data out

Run `python -m frontier_connectors import rescale <job id> --out ds` with RESCALE_API_KEY set (RESCALE_API_URL or api_url= for eu.rescale.com / platform.rescale.jp; --dry-run prints the calls). Or pass a <name>.rescale.json reference file. Or download the job files in the web UI and convert that directory: each file goes to the matching connector.

## Requirements and licence

Licence: Apache-2.0.

# frontier-connector-simulink

Reads Simulink and Simscape logs, FMU results (FMI CSV, Dymola / OpenModelica MAT) and FMU and SLX metadata. FMUs are never executed; MATLAB objects need the +frontier export package.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install simulink
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info simulink
```

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors describe run.mat          # or Model_res.mat, result.csv, Model.fmu, model.slx
python -m frontier_connectors convert run.mat --out dataset
```

A system simulation has no geometry: every run on one time base becomes a `point_cloud` sample
with one point at the origin and one field per signal (`[time, point, component]`). Units, block
paths, port indices, sample times, interpolation, data types, FMI causality and variability and
aliases are in `metadata["signals"][name]`; run parameters in `metadata["parameters"]`.

| Source | Read |
| --- | --- |
| `frontier.exportSimulink`, `exportSDI`, `exportSimulinkSignals` MAT-file | yes, through the `matlab` connector (one zone per time base) |
| `frontier.exportSimulinkRuns` folder (`frontier_runs.json` + one file per run) | yes, one sample per run with its parameters |
| Simulink "Structure with time", "Structure", "Array" (`tout` + `yout` / `xout`), To File arrays (MAT v5, v7, v7.3) | yes |
| `Simulink.SimulationOutput`, `Dataset` (`logsout`), `timeseries`, `timetable`, `Signal`, `simscape.logging.Node` (`simlog`), SDI objects in a MAT-file | no: detected by class; `NeedsExportError` names the variable, the class and the MATLAB call |
| FMI CSV results (FMPy `--output-file`, FMI Cross-Check `*_ref.csv` / `*_out.csv`, OpenModelica CSV) | yes; units and descriptions from the FMU next to the file |
| Dymola / OpenModelica `*_res.mat` (trajectory 1.0 and 1.1, binTrans and binNormal) | yes; alias signs, parameters, units from Dymola descriptions; memory-mapped |
| `.fmu`, unpacked FMU, `modelDescription.xml` (FMI 1.0, 2.0, 3.0) | variable catalogue and default experiment; a result file next to it is read. No FMU is executed |
| `.slx`, `.mdl` | package metadata, solver and logging settings; `read` raises `NeedsExportError` |

`detect` claims a `.mat` or `.csv` file only on a Simulink, FMI or trajectory-file marker. Other
files stay with `matlab` or `tabular`; force this connector with `--connector simulink`.

Options: `events` (`last` | `first` | `keep`: which record of a repeated instant is kept),
`aliases` (trajectory files: alias variables as fields of their own), `fmu`, `result` (pair a
result with a model description), `to_file` (name of a To File array), `time`, `delimiter`
(CSV), `mapping` (canonical files, passed to the `matlab` connector, for example
`{"resample": true}`).

In MATLAB, add the folder printed by `python -m frontier_connectors exporters matlab` to the path:

```matlab
frontier.exportSimulink(sim('model'), 'run.mat');             % logsout, yout, xout, simlog
frontier.exportSimulinkRuns(parsim(in), 'runs', 'Inputs', in); % one sample per run
frontier.exportSDI('all', 'sdi.mat');                         % Simulation Data Inspector runs
```

## Status

`verified-public-sample`. Reads FMI CSV results with units from the FMU's modelDescription.xml (FMI 1.0, 2.0 and 3.0), Dymola 7.4 / 2012 and OpenModelica 1.8 result files (trajectory 1.1 binTrans and binNormal, 1.0 'save plotted') including alias signs and parameters, and SLX package metadata. Validated on generated files only: Simulink 'Structure with time', 'Structure' and 'Array' logs, To File arrays, .mdl files, and detection of Simulink, timeseries and Simscape objects. frontier.exportSimulink, exportSDI and exportSimulinkRuns are not validated under MATLAB. MATLAB objects (SimulationOutput, Dataset, timeseries, simlog) are not decoded: read raises NeedsExportError with the exporter call. FMUs are never executed.

## Getting the data out

Simulink: add the folder printed by `python -m frontier_connectors exporters matlab` to the MATLAB path, then frontier.exportSimulink(sim(model), 'run.mat') (logsout, yout, xout, To Workspace, Simscape simlog), frontier.exportSimulinkRuns(parsim(in), 'runs') for several runs, frontier.exportSDI('all', 'sdi.mat') for Simulation Data Inspector runs. Logs saved as 'Structure with time' / 'Array' are read directly. FMUs: simulate with an FMI tool and keep the result next to the FMU (FMPy: `fmpy simulate m.fmu --output-file m_out.csv`; Dymola / OpenModelica: the *_res.mat result file).

## Requirements and licence

Licence: Apache-2.0.

Run `starccm+ -batch ExportForFrontier.java case.sim` (macro: `python -m frontier_connectors exporters starccm`); it writes EnSight Gold or CGNS plus frontier_export.json. # frontier-connector-tabular

Reads CSV, TSV and text tables, Parquet, and OpenFOAM probes and force coefficients. Parquet needs pyarrow.

## Install

```bash
python -m frontier_connectors plugins install tabular
python -m frontier_connectors plugins info tabular
```

## Status

`verified-public-sample`. Layouts: point snapshot, long (time, probe) tables, time + signal columns. Global signals are stored on one point at the origin. Parquet needs pyarrow. ParaView, Fluent, CFX and COMSOL style tables and Parquet are validated on generated files only. Tecplot ASCII and COMSOL '% Model:' files belong to their own connectors. Date-string time columns and ragged probe series (without per_probe) are not supported.

ParaView: File > Save Data > CSV (point data). Fluent: File > Export > ASCII, or report-file monitors (.out). CFX / COMSOL / STAR-CCM+: export monitor or probe tables as CSV/text.
